mechanism: oracle fixture (task-oracle3, 2026-09-05): compose the two primitives the first two oracle runs tested in isolation. `forbid_heavy_cargo!` writes the standing ban FIRST (it only needs the schedule to resolve the robot name, and a preceding release can invalidate the very slots that name resolution walks), then `release_pending_assignments!` creates the candidate assignment edges the ban can bind to. surface=sched because the body edits the schedule graph; the harness re-solve (_resolve_if_needed!) then formulates the MILP with BOTH the freed edges and the standing ban.
impl_code:
function OracleLightenAndRelease!(env)
    BATTERY_FLEET[] === nothing && return (; status = :no_battery_info)
    rid = ood_event_target()
    rid === nothing && return (; status = :no_target)
    ban = forbid_heavy_cargo!(env; agent = string(rid), n = 3)
    ban.status === :banned || return ban
    inv = build_invariant(env)
    edges = release_pending_assignments!(env, inv; agent = string(rid))
    edges isa AbstractVector || return edges
    return (; status = :released, removed = length(edges))
end
